description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for three metrics: Δ Accuracy, Initial Accuracy, and a baseline represented by the grey bar. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” ranges from 0.86 to 1.00 in linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The “Δ Accuracy” line, shown in orange with diamond markers and a dashed line, starts at approximately 0.25 at an initial confidence of 0.86, decreases to a minimum of about 0.05 at 0.95, then rises slightly to about 0.20 at 1.00. The “Initial Accuracy” line, shown in green with square markers and a dashed line, begins at approximately 0.65 at 0.86, rises to a peak of about 0.90 at 0.97, then declines to about 0.75 at 1.00. The blue line with circular markers and solid line, representing the baseline, remains nearly constant at approximately 0.98 across the entire range of initial confidence from 0.86 to 1.00.
